Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. Tamerlan Tsarnaev told a photographer: "God said no alcohol. There are no values anymore... people can't control themselves." A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about terrorism, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative [[Peter T. The Federal Bureau of Investigation, which has been investigating the attack along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."
thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.

Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."
The FBI reports that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left

A person who was briefed on the investigation said at least one of the devices was made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators have found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. Tamerlan Tsarnaev told a photographer: "God said no alcohol. There are no values anymore... people can't control themselves." A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about radical Islamism 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about radical Islamism 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.

The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]], which has been investigating the attack along with the [[Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives]] (ATF), the [[Central Intelligence Agency]], and the [[National Counterterrorism Center]],<ref name="Hosenball">{{cite web| url=http://www.globalpost.com/dispatch/news/thomson-reuters/130415/investigators-scour-video-photos-boston-marathon-bomb-clues |title=Investigators scour video, photos for Boston Marathon bomb clues|last1=Hosenball| first1=Mark |first2=Svea| last2=Herbst-Bayliss |date=April 16, 2013|work=[[GlobalPost]]|publisher=[[Thomson Reuters]] |accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.<ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/fbi-releases-video-of-boston-bombing-suspects.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | title = FBI Posts Images of Pair Suspected in Boston Attack | newspaper = The NY Times | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref>

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative [[Peter T. King|Peter King]], member of the [[United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence|House Intelligence Committee]] said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."<ref>{{cite web|title=Live updates: Obama calls Boston bombings a 'heinous, cowardly' act of terror |url=http://www.latimes.com/news/nation/nationnow/la-na-nn-boston-searches-for-clues-to-bombing-that-killed-3-injured-176-20130416,0,318317.story?page=2 |work=LA Times|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>
[[File:FBI and JTTF at Boston bombing.jpg|thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.]]

Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".<ref>{{cite web|title=Injured Saudi man not a suspect in Boston attacks|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579893/sources-injured-saudi-man-not-a-suspect-in-boston-attacks/|last=Sison |first=Bree|publisher=CBS News|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Nelson|first=Steven|title=Boston Police: 'We Are Questioning Many People'|url=http://www.usnews.com/news/newsgram/articles/2013/04/15/boston-police-we-are-questioning-many-people |accessdate=April 16, 2013|newspaper=[[U.S. News & World Report]]}}</ref><ref name="Hunter">{{cite web|url= http://livewire.talkingpointsmemo.com/entry/boston-police-commissioner-there-is-no-suspect-in|title=Boston Police Commissioner: 'There Is No Suspect In Custody'|last=Hunter|first=Walker|date=April 16, 2013|publisher=[[Talking Points Memo]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."<ref name="CNN_FBI">{{cite news|title=FBI will try to rebuild Boston bombs|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/15/us/boston-marathon-investigation/index.html|last=Smith |first=Matt|coauthors=Josh Levs|publisher=CNN|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Large police presence in Revere connected to Boston bombing|url=http://www.myfoxboston.com/story/21986273/large-police-presence-in-revere-connected-to-boston-bombing |publisher=[[WFXT]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>
[[File:Pressure cooker bomb.jpg|The FBI reports that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left]]

A person who was briefed on the investigation said at least one of the devices was made from a [[pressure cooker]] packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack.<ref name="CNN_FBI"/> The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ellement|first=John|title=Boston Medical Center reports five-year-old boy in critical condition, 23 victims treated from Boston Marathon bombings|url=http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/17/boston-medical-center-reports-five-year-old-boy-critical-condition-victims-treated-from-boston-marathon-bombings/gkKXBTqL2jyNhsC2Kz5GyO/story.html|accessdate=April 17, 2013|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=April 17, 2013|author2=Brian Ballou}}</ref> Investigators have found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579766/boston-marathon-bombings-suburban-apartment-searched/ |title=FBI seeks images in Boston Marathon bomb probe; new details emerge on explosives |work=CBS News|date=April 16, 2013|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> [[Gunpowder]] was most likely used in the explosive devices.<ref name="Lister">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/16/us/boston-marathon-lone-wolf/|title=Boston Marathon bombs similar to 'lone wolf' devices, experts say|last=Lister|first=Tim|coauthors=Paul Cruickshank|date=April 17, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref>

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos by Feiz Mohammad, a Wahhabist Muslim cleric who has expressed fundamentalist beliefs. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative [[Peter T. Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation, which has been investigating the attack along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."

The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19.

thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation, which has been investigating the attack along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."

The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). 

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19.

Investigation.wikitext:
[[File:FBI and JTTF at Boston bombing.jpg|thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.]]
The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]], which has been investigating the attack along with the [[Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives]] (ATF), the [[Central Intelligence Agency]], and the [[National Counterterrorism Center]],<ref name="Hosenball">{{cite web| url=http://www.globalpost.com/dispatch/news/thomson-reuters/130415/investigators-scour-video-photos-boston-marathon-bomb-clues |title=Investigators scour video, photos for Boston Marathon bomb clues|last1=Hosenball| first1=Mark |first2=Svea| last2=Herbst-Bayliss |date=April 16, 2013|work=[[GlobalPost]]|publisher=[[Thomson Reuters]] |accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.<ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/fbi-releases-video-of-boston-bombing-suspects.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | title = FBI Posts Images of Pair Suspected in Boston Attack | newspaper = The NY Times | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref>

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative [[Peter T. King|Peter King]], member of the [[United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence|House Intelligence Committee]] said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."<ref>{{cite web|title=Live updates: Obama calls Boston bombings a 'heinous, cowardly' act of terror |url=http://www.latimes.com/news/nation/nationnow/la-na-nn-boston-searches-for-clues-to-bombing-that-killed-3-injured-176-20130416,0,318317.story?page=2 |work=LA Times|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Pressure cooker bomb.jpg|The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left]]
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".<ref>{{cite web|title=Injured Saudi man not a suspect in Boston attacks|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579893/sources-injured-saudi-man-not-a-suspect-in-boston-attacks/|last=Sison |first=Bree|publisher=CBS News|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Nelson|first=Steven|title=Boston Police: 'We Are Questioning Many People'|url=http://www.usnews.com/news/newsgram/articles/2013/04/15/boston-police-we-are-questioning-many-people |accessdate=April 16, 2013|newspaper=[[U.S. News & World Report]]}}</ref><ref name="Hunter">{{cite web|url= http://livewire.talkingpointsmemo.com/entry/boston-police-commissioner-there-is-no-suspect-in|title=Boston Police Commissioner: 'There Is No Suspect In Custody'|last=Hunter|first=Walker|date=April 16, 2013|publisher=[[Talking Points Memo]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."<ref name="CNN_FBI">{{cite news|title=FBI will try to rebuild Boston bombs|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/15/us/boston-marathon-investigation/index.html|last=Smith |first=Matt|coauthors=Josh Levs|publisher=CNN|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Large police presence in Revere connected to Boston bombing|url=http://www.myfoxboston.com/story/21986273/large-police-presence-in-revere-connected-to-boston-bombing |publisher=[[WFXT]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a [[pressure cooker]] packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack.<ref name="CNN_FBI"/> The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ellement|first=John|title=Boston Medical Center reports five-year-old boy in critical condition, 23 victims treated from Boston Marathon bombings|url=http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/17/boston-medical-center-reports-five-year-old-boy-critical-condition-victims-treated-from-boston-marathon-bombings/gkKXBTqL2jyNhsC2Kz5GyO/story.html|accessdate=April 17, 2013|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=April 17, 2013|author2=Brian Ballou}}</ref> Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579766/boston-marathon-bombings-suburban-apartment-searched/ |title=FBI seeks images in Boston Marathon bomb probe; new details emerge on explosives |work=CBS News|date=April 16, 2013|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> [[Gunpowder]] was most likely used in the explosive devices.<ref name="Lister">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/16/us/boston-marathon-lone-wolf/|title=Boston Marathon bombs similar to 'lone wolf' devices, experts say|last=Lister|first=Tim|coauthors=Paul Cruickshank|date=April 17, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref>

Investigation.plaintext:
thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation, which has been investigating the attack along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."

The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). 

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Investigation.plaintext:
thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation, which has been investigating the attack along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."

The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). 

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). 

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a US permanent resident. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation, which has been investigating the attack along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."

The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). 

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). 

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation, which has been investigating the attack along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, was treating the bombings as a terrorist attack, with at least two alleged perpetrators so far having been officially identified.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."

The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Investigation.plaintext:
thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation, led the attack investigating along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, treating the bombings as a terrorist attack and naming two alleged perpetrators officially as suspects.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."

The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan, he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan, he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Other people identified or arrested as suspects
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car.

The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]], led the attack investigating along with the [[Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives]] (ATF), the [[Central Intelligence Agency]], and the [[National Counterterrorism Center]],<ref name="Hosenball">{{cite web| url=http://www.globalpost.com/dispatch/news/thomson-reuters/130415/investigators-scour-video-photos-boston-marathon-bomb-clues |title=Investigators scour video, photos for Boston Marathon bomb clues|last1=Hosenball| first1=Mark |first2=Svea| last2=Herbst-Bayliss |date=April 16, 2013|work=[[GlobalPost]]|publisher=[[Thomson Reuters]] |accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> treating the bombings as a terrorist attack and naming two alleged perpetrators officially as suspects.<ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/fbi-releases-video-of-boston-bombing-suspects.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | title = FBI Posts Images of Pair Suspected in Boston Attack | newspaper = The NY Times | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref>

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative [[Peter T. King|Peter King]], member of the [[United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence|House Intelligence Committee]] said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."<ref>{{cite web|title=Live updates: Obama calls Boston bombings a 'heinous, cowardly' act of terror |url=http://www.latimes.com/news/nation/nationnow/la-na-nn-boston-searches-for-clues-to-bombing-that-killed-3-injured-176-20130416,0,318317.story?page=2 |work=LA Times|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Pressure cooker bomb.jpg|The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left]]
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".<ref>{{cite web|title=Injured Saudi man not a suspect in Boston attacks|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579893/sources-injured-saudi-man-not-a-suspect-in-boston-attacks/|last=Sison |first=Bree|publisher=CBS News|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Nelson|first=Steven|title=Boston Police: 'We Are Questioning Many People'|url=http://www.usnews.com/news/newsgram/articles/2013/04/15/boston-police-we-are-questioning-many-people |accessdate=April 16, 2013|newspaper=[[U.S. News & World Report]]}}</ref><ref name="Hunter">{{cite web|url= http://livewire.talkingpointsmemo.com/entry/boston-police-commissioner-there-is-no-suspect-in|title=Boston Police Commissioner: 'There Is No Suspect In Custody'|last=Hunter|first=Walker|date=April 16, 2013|publisher=[[Talking Points Memo]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."<ref name="CNN_FBI">{{cite news|title=FBI will try to rebuild Boston bombs|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/15/us/boston-marathon-investigation/index.html|last=Smith |first=Matt|coauthors=Josh Levs|publisher=CNN|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Large police presence in Revere connected to Boston bombing|url=http://www.myfoxboston.com/story/21986273/large-police-presence-in-revere-connected-to-boston-bombing |publisher=[[WFXT]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a [[pressure cooker]] packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack.<ref name="CNN_FBI"/> The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ellement|first=John|title=Boston Medical Center reports five-year-old boy in critical condition, 23 victims treated from Boston Marathon bombings|url=http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/17/boston-medical-center-reports-five-year-old-boy-critical-condition-victims-treated-from-boston-marathon-bombings/gkKXBTqL2jyNhsC2Kz5GyO/story.html|accessdate=April 17, 2013|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=April 17, 2013|author2=Brian Ballou}}</ref> Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579766/boston-marathon-bombings-suburban-apartment-searched/ |title=FBI seeks images in Boston Marathon bomb probe; new details emerge on explosives |work=CBS News|date=April 16, 2013|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> [[Gunpowder]] was most likely used in the explosive devices.<ref name="Lister">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/16/us/boston-marathon-lone-wolf/|title=Boston Marathon bombs similar to 'lone wolf' devices, experts say|last=Lister|first=Tim|coauthors=Paul Cruickshank|date=April 17, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref>

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan, he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Other people identified or arrested as suspects
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car. Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.
