When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police.<ref>{{cite news|title=Watertown family finds alleged marathon bomber in boat|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/watertown-family-finds-alleged-marathon-bomber-boat/y3te9bJyaatLpd4yvLGRGJ/story.html|author=Anderson, Derek J.|date=April 19, 2013|work=Boston Globe|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through [[thermal imaging]] cameras.<ref name="captured" /> He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff,<ref name=autogenerated2 /><ref name=autogenerated1 /> and transported to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]] where he was listed in [[serious condition]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-we-got-him-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive | title = 'We got him!': Boston bombing suspect captured alive | place = US | newspaper = News | publisher = NBC | date = 2013‐4‐19}}.</ref>

Dzokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a [[Miranda warning]], as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "[[public safety exception]]".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2013/04/next-for-bombing-suspect-high-value-detainee-interrogation-group/ |title=Feds Make Miranda Rights Exception for Marathon Bombing Suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev |work=[[ABC News]] |date=April 19, 2013 }}</ref>

===Other people identified or arrested as suspects===
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.3news.co.nz/LIVE-UPDATES-Police-hunt-for-Boston-bombing-suspect/tabid/417/articleID/294897/Default.aspx| title=LIVE UPDATES: Police hunt Boston bombing suspect| publisher=News 3 (New Zealand)| date=April 20, 2013}}</ref> Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.masslive.com/news/index.ssf/2013/04/reports_police_arrest_3_in_new.html| title=Police take 3 into custody in New Bedford at housing complex where Boston bombing suspect may have lived| publisher=MassLive.com| date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>
Suspects.plaintext:
Initial identification 
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer training at the Team Lowell Club. He was 2010 New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and winner of the Rocky Marciano Trophy.<ref name="deadspin"> He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan, he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture
thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition.

Dzokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Other people identified or arrested as suspects
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car. Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.

Investigation.wikitext:
[[File:FBI and JTTF at Boston bombing.jpg|thumb|Richard DesLauriers, special agent in charge of the FBI Boston Field Office, addresses the media.]]
The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]], led the attack investigating along with the [[Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives]] (ATF), the [[Central Intelligence Agency]], and the [[National Counterterrorism Center]],<ref name="Hosenball">{{cite web| url=http://www.globalpost.com/dispatch/news/thomson-reuters/130415/investigators-scour-video-photos-boston-marathon-bomb-clues |title=Investigators scour video, photos for Boston Marathon bomb clues|last1=Hosenball| first1=Mark |first2=Svea| last2=Herbst-Bayliss |date=April 16, 2013|work=[[GlobalPost]]|publisher=[[Thomson Reuters]] |accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> treating the bombings as a terrorist attack and naming two alleged perpetrators officially as suspects.<ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/fbi-releases-video-of-boston-bombing-suspects.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | title = FBI Posts Images of Pair Suspected in Boston Attack | newspaper = The NY Times | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref>

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative [[Peter T. King|Peter King]], member of the [[United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence|House Intelligence Committee]] said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."<ref>{{cite web|title=Live updates: Obama calls Boston bombings a 'heinous, cowardly' act of terror |url=http://www.latimes.com/news/nation/nationnow/la-na-nn-boston-searches-for-clues-to-bombing-that-killed-3-injured-176-20130416,0,318317.story?page=2 |work=LA Times|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Pressure cooker bomb.jpg|The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left]]
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".<ref>{{cite web|title=Injured Saudi man not a suspect in Boston attacks|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579893/sources-injured-saudi-man-not-a-suspect-in-boston-attacks/|last=Sison |first=Bree|publisher=CBS News|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Nelson|first=Steven|title=Boston Police: 'We Are Questioning Many People'|url=http://www.usnews.com/news/newsgram/articles/2013/04/15/boston-police-we-are-questioning-many-people |accessdate=April 16, 2013|newspaper=[[U.S. News & World Report]]}}</ref><ref name="Hunter">{{cite web|url= http://livewire.talkingpointsmemo.com/entry/boston-police-commissioner-there-is-no-suspect-in|title=Boston Police Commissioner: 'There Is No Suspect In Custody'|last=Hunter|first=Walker|date=April 16, 2013|publisher=[[Talking Points Memo]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."<ref name="CNN_FBI">{{cite news|title=FBI will try to rebuild Boston bombs|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/15/us/boston-marathon-investigation/index.html|last=Smith |first=Matt|coauthors=Josh Levs|publisher=CNN|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Large police presence in Revere connected to Boston bombing|url=http://www.myfoxboston.com/story/21986273/large-police-presence-in-revere-connected-to-boston-bombing |publisher=[[WFXT]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a [[pressure cooker]] packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack.<ref name="CNN_FBI"/> The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ellement|first=John|title=Boston Medical Center reports five-year-old boy in critical condition, 23 victims treated from Boston Marathon bombings|url=http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/17/boston-medical-center-reports-five-year-old-boy-critical-condition-victims-treated-from-boston-marathon-bombings/gkKXBTqL2jyNhsC2Kz5GyO/story.html|accessdate=April 17, 2013|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=April 17, 2013|author2=Brian Ballou}}</ref> Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579766/boston-marathon-bombings-suburban-apartment-searched/ |title=FBI seeks images in Boston Marathon bomb probe; new details emerge on explosives |work=CBS News|date=April 16, 2013|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> [[Gunpowder]] was most likely used in the explosive devices.<ref name="Lister">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/16/us/boston-marathon-lone-wolf/|title=Boston Marathon bombs similar to 'lone wolf' devices, experts say|last=Lister|first=Tim|coauthors=Paul Cruickshank|date=April 17, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref>

The Federal Bureau of Investigation, led the attack investigating along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Counterterrorism Center, treating the bombings as a terrorist attack and naming two alleged perpetrators officially as suspects.

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative Peter King, member of the House Intelligence Committee said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."

The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a pressure cooker packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack. The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop. Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb. Gunpowder was most likely used in the explosive devices.

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them.<ref name='FBI18AprSuspectPics'>{{cite web |url= http://www.fbi.gov/news/updates-on-investigation-into-multiple-explosions-in-boston/updates-on-investigation-into-multiple-explosions-in-boston |title=Updates on Investigation Into Multiple Explosions in Boston — Video and Photos Released in Bombings Case |accessdate=April 18, 2013 |date=Apr 18, 2013 |work=The FBI Federal Bureau of Investigation |publisher= Department of Justice | place = US}}</ref><ref name="CNN_Smith">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/18/us/boston-blasts/index.html |title= FBI: Help us ID Boston bomb suspects|last1 = Smith|first1 = Matthew 'Matt' | first2 = Thomas 'Thom' | last2 = Patterson|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.<ref>{{cite news | title=FBI Releases Images of Two Suspects in Boston Attack|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-set-to-mourn-bombing-victims.html?pagewanted=all|accessdate=April 18, 2013|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 18, 2013}}</ref> Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.<ref>http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/</ref>

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
*'''Tamerlan Tsarnaev''', 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 ([[Cyrillic script]]: Тамерлан Царнаев)
*'''Dzhokhar Tsarnaev''', 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013">{{cite web | last = Abad-Santos | first = Alexander | title = Who Is Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the Man at the Center of the Boston Manhunt? | publisher = The Atlantic | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/who-is-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-boston/64382/ | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>

Ethnic [[Chechens]] from the [[North Caucasus]], they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002<ref name="NYTimes04192013" /><ref>{{cite news |url=http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887324493704578432030609754740.html |title=Boston Bombing Suspect Killed in Shootout|date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Wall Street Journal |first1=Evan |last1=Perez |first2=Jennifer |last2=Smith |first3=Pervaiz |last3=Shallwani |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html|title=One Boston Bombing Suspect Is Dead, Second at Large; Area on Lockdown|date=April 19, 2013|newspaper= The New York Times| first1 =Katharine Q | last1 = Seelye | first2 = Michael | last2 = Cooper}}</ref><ref name="captured">{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/ |title= 'Captured!!!' Boston police announce Marathon bombing suspect in custody| first1 = Chelsea J | last1 = Carter | first2 = Gregory ‘Greg’ | last2 = Botelho|date=April 20, 2013|work= [[CNN]]}}</ref> and had been living in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], for the past ten years.<ref name = "AtlanticWire04192013" />  They had previously lived in [[Tokmok]], [[Kyrgyzstan]], and [[Makhachkala]], [[Dagestan]], [[Russia]].<ref name="WashPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Finn | first = Peter | title =  Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal conflict | publisher = Washington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="SullivanAP04192013">{{cite news | last = Sullivan | first = Eileen | title =  Manhunt in Boston after bombing suspect is killed | agency = Associated Press | date = April 19, 2013 | url =  http://apnews.myway.com/article/20130419/DA5OPNCO2.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  Both brothers are [[Muslims]].<ref name="HuffPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Kaleem | first = Jaweed | title = Boston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing  | publisher = Huffington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/04/19/boston-bombing-suspects-muslim_n_3116299.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="HuffPostNoronha04192013">{{cite web | last = Noronha | first = Charmaine | title = Aunt says US suspect recently became devout Muslim | publisher = Huffington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.huffingtonpost.com/huff-wires/20130419/cn-canada-boston-marathon-suspects-aunt/# | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="NYTimes04192013">{{cite news | last = Goode | first = Erica | title =  Brothers Seen as Good Students and Avid Athletes | publisher = New York Times | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/details-of-tsarnaev-brothers-boston-suspects-emerge.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.<ref>{{Citation | newspaper = News | publisher = NBC | place = New York | url = http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html | title = Boston marathon bombing suspects}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title =Boston manhunt for bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev– live updates|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-mit-police-dead-watertown|accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper= The Guardian | place = UK}}</ref><ref name="AtlanticWire04192013" /><ref name="ForeignPolicy04192013" />  He was born in the [[Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic|Russian SFSR]] in the [[Soviet Union]].<ref name="WPostGowen04192013">{{Citation | last = Gowen | first = Annie | last2 = Horwitz | first2 = Sari | last3 = Markon | first3 = Jerry | title = Boston lockdown lifted; marathon bombing suspect still at large | newspaper = [[Washington Post]] | year = 2013 | date = April 19 | url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/world/national-security/massive-police-operation-under-way-in-boston/2013/04/19/979ec6dc-a8c6-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_print.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref> He was a well-known [[boxing|boxer]] training at the Team Lowell Club. He was 2010 New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and winner of the Rocky Marciano Trophy.<ref name="deadspin">{{Citation | last = Burke | first = Thimothy | title = Everything we know about Tamerlan Tsarnaev, dead bombing suspect | newspaper = Deadspin | year = 2013 | date = April 19 | url = http://deadspin.com/heres-everything-we-know-about-tamerlan-tsarnaev-the-476415081 | accessdate = April 20, 2013 }}</ref> One of his ambitions according to a report published ''The Comment'', the [[Boston University Graduate School Magazine, Tamerlan declared he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time, to be selected for the US Olympic team. He added would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia".<ref name="deadspin"/> He had been arrested in 2009 for [[domestic assault]] and [[Battery (crime)|battery]] after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.<ref name="ForeignPolicy04192013"> {{cite web | last = Kenner | first = David | title = Who Is Tamerlan Tsarnaev | publisher = Foreign Policy | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://blog.foreignpolicy.com/posts/2013/04/19/who_is_tamerlan_tzarnaev? | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  He was not an American citizen, but was a US [[Permanent residence (United States)|permanent resident]].<ref name="captured" />

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013.<ref name=autogenerated2>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (Update: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher= Mediaite|accessdate= April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-mit-police-dead-watertown | title = Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive | type = live updates | newspaper = The Guardian | accessdate = April 20, 2013 | year = 2013 | month = Apr}}.</ref> At the time of the incident, he was a student at the [[University of Massachusetts Dartmouth]], with a major in [[marine biology]].<ref name=guard_tsarnaev>{{cite news|title=Dzhokhar Tsarnaev: Boston bombing suspect was pupil at Cambridge high school|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-suspect-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-school| place = UK | newspaper= The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/national/boston-marathon-suspects-tamerlan-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-appeared-lead-normal-lives-article-1.1321715|title=Boston Marathon suspects Tamerlan, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev: Brothers appeared to lead normal lives|newspaper=New York Daily News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/19/bombing-suspect-attended-umass-dartmouth-prompting-school-closure-college-friend-shocked-charge-boston-marathon-bomber/YcEDA5nvNDi0T1jJTNjKiP/story.html|title=Bombing suspect attended UMass Dartmouth, prompting school closure; college friend shocked by charge he is Boston Marathon bomber|newspaper=boston.com}}</ref> He was also an avid [[wrestling|wrestler]] and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan,<ref name="WPostGowen04192013" /> he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.<ref name="captured" />  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in [[Montgomery Village, Maryland]], pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Marathon bombers: suspect Dzhozkar Tsarnaev's uncle Ruslan Tsarni pleads 'turn yourself in'|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/northamerica/usa/10006657/Boston-Marathon-bombers-suspect-Dzhozkar-Tsarnaevs-uncle-Ruslan-Tsarni-pleads-turn-yourself-in.html| place = UK | agency=Associated Press|date=April 19, 2013|work=The Telegraph|publisher=Telegraph Media|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

===Manhunt and capture===
[[File:Tamerlan-and-Dzokhar-Tsarnaev-suspect-photos.jpg|thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings]]
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department]] officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven | first = Stephanie|date = April 19, 2013|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url =http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near the [[Stata Center]] (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web| url = http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |publisher=Boston Globe|title= Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1 =Shelley | last1 = Murphy | first2 = Milton J |last2 = Valencia | first3 = Wesley | last3 = Lowery | first4 = Akilah | last4 = Johnson | first5 = Eric | last5 = Moskowitz | first6 = Lisa | last6 = Wangsness | first7 = John R | last7 = Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url = http://emergency.mit.net/emergency | publisher = MIT | title = Emergency Information | date = April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name = SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye | first1 = Katherine Q | last2 = Cooper | first2 = Michael|date= April 19, 2013|  work = The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.<ref>{{cite web|last=Finn|first=Peter|title=Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal Chechen conflict|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html|publisher=''The Washington Post''|accessdate=April 20, 2013|coauthors=Carol D. Leonnig and Will Englund|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |author=Seelye, K. Q.; Rashbaum, W. K. and Cooper, M.|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts]].<ref name="captured" /> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-22212946|title=Boston Marathon bomb suspect still at large|publisher=''[[BBC]]''|date=April 20, 2013|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and was taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan|first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", was "still at large".<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url =http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Early on April 19, Watertown residents received [[reverse 911]] calls asking them to stay indoors.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/watertown/2013/04/officials_in_watertown_field_c.html | year = 2013 | month = Apr | title = Officials in Watertown field calls from worried residents – Watertown – Your Town | newspaper = Boston}}.</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in [[Dagestan]], encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Cite web | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref> [[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=(7) IEDs have been recovered|url=http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/|publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]], and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan International Airport]] remained open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry,<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Bomb Suspect Captured Alive in Backyard Boat|url=http://abcnews.go.com/US/one-boston-marathon-suspect-dead-second-run-police-say/story?id=18994511|author=Thomas, Pierre; Ross, Brian; Ferran, Lee; Curry, Colleen|date=April 19, 2013|work=ABC News|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St.<ref>{{cite news|title=Second Boston Marathon bombing suspect in custody|url=http://www.wcvb.com/Second-Boston-Marathon-bombing-suspect-in-custody/-/9849586/19814816/-/cw8b4az/-/index.html|date=April 20, 2013|work=WCBV.com|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police.<ref>{{cite news|title=Watertown family finds alleged marathon bomber in boat|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/watertown-family-finds-alleged-marathon-bomber-boat/y3te9bJyaatLpd4yvLGRGJ/story.html|author=Anderson, Derek J.|date=April 19, 2013|work=Boston Globe|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through [[thermal imaging]] cameras.<ref name="captured" /> He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff,<ref name=autogenerated2 /><ref name=autogenerated1 /> and transported to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]] where he was listed in [[serious condition]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-we-got-him-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive | title = 'We got him!': Boston bombing suspect captured alive | place = US | newspaper = News | publisher = NBC | date = 2013‐4‐19}}.</ref>

Dzokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a [[Miranda warning]], as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "[[public safety exception]]".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2013/04/next-for-bombing-suspect-high-value-detainee-interrogation-group/ |title=Feds Make Miranda Rights Exception for Marathon Bombing Suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev |work=[[ABC News]] |date=April 19, 2013 }}</ref>

===Other people identified or arrested as suspects===
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.3news.co.nz/LIVE-UPDATES-Police-hunt-for-Boston-bombing-suspect/tabid/417/articleID/294897/Default.aspx| title=LIVE UPDATES: Police hunt Boston bombing suspect| publisher=News 3 (New Zealand)| date=April 20, 2013}}</ref> Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.masslive.com/news/index.ssf/2013/04/reports_police_arrest_3_in_new.html| title=Police take 3 into custody in New Bedford at housing complex where Boston bombing suspect may have lived| publisher=MassLive.com| date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Initial identification 
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer training at the Team Lowell Club. He was 2010 New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and winner of the Rocky Marciano Trophy. One of his ambitions according to a report published The Comment, the [[Boston University Graduate School Magazine, Tamerlan declared he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time, to be selected for the US Olympic team. He added would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia". He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan, he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture
thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition.

Dzokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Other people identified or arrested as suspects
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car. Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.

Suspects.plaintext:
Initial identification 
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев), 26-years old, born October 21, 1986
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев), 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993.

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The Tsranaevs also had two daughters, Bella and Amina. Tameraln and Dzhokhar emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer training at the Wai Kru Mixed Martial Arts 
Center, a Lowell club. He was 2010 New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and winner of the Rocky Marciano Trophy. One of his ambitions according to a report published in The Comment, the Boston University Graduate Student Magazine of Boston University's College of Communications, Tamerlan declared he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time, to be selected for the US Olympic team. He added would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia". He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan, he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture
thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Other people identified or arrested as suspects
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car. Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.

The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]], led the attack investigating along with the [[Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives]] (ATF), the [[Central Intelligence Agency]], and the [[National Counterterrorism Center]],<ref name="Hosenball">{{cite web| url=http://www.globalpost.com/dispatch/news/thomson-reuters/130415/investigators-scour-video-photos-boston-marathon-bomb-clues |title=Investigators scour video, photos for Boston Marathon bomb clues|last1=Hosenball| first1=Mark |first2=Svea| last2=Herbst-Bayliss |date=April 16, 2013|work=[[GlobalPost]]|publisher=[[Thomson Reuters]] |accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> treating the bombings as a terrorist attack and naming two alleged perpetrators officially as suspects.<ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/fbi-releases-video-of-boston-bombing-suspects.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | title = FBI Posts Images of Pair Suspected in Boston Attack | newspaper = The NY Times | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref>

United States government officials stated that there had been no intelligence reports that indicated such a bombing would take place. Representative [[Peter T. King|Peter King]], member of the [[United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence|House Intelligence Committee]] said: "I received two top secret briefings last week on the current threat levels in the United States, and there was no evidence of this at all."<ref>{{cite web|title=Live updates: Obama calls Boston bombings a 'heinous, cowardly' act of terror |url=http://www.latimes.com/news/nation/nationnow/la-na-nn-boston-searches-for-clues-to-bombing-that-killed-3-injured-176-20130416,0,318317.story?page=2 |work=LA Times|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Pressure cooker bomb.jpg|The FBI reported that this pressure cooker fragment is part of one of the explosive devices.|thumb|left]]
Though not treated as suspects, several people who were near the scene of the blast and the surrounding area were taken into custody and questioned about the bombings, including a Saudi man that police stopped as he was walking away from the explosion, and detained when some of his responses to questions "made them uncomfortable".<ref>{{cite web|title=Injured Saudi man not a suspect in Boston attacks|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579893/sources-injured-saudi-man-not-a-suspect-in-boston-attacks/|last=Sison |first=Bree|publisher=CBS News|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Nelson|first=Steven|title=Boston Police: 'We Are Questioning Many People'|url=http://www.usnews.com/news/newsgram/articles/2013/04/15/boston-police-we-are-questioning-many-people |accessdate=April 16, 2013|newspaper=[[U.S. News & World Report]]}}</ref><ref name="Hunter">{{cite web|url= http://livewire.talkingpointsmemo.com/entry/boston-police-commissioner-there-is-no-suspect-in|title=Boston Police Commissioner: 'There Is No Suspect In Custody'|last=Hunter|first=Walker|date=April 16, 2013|publisher=[[Talking Points Memo]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>  Law enforcement searched his residence in a Boston suburb, but CNN later reported that he was found to have no connection to the attack, with an unnamed U.S. official saying "he was just at the wrong place at the wrong time."<ref name="CNN_FBI">{{cite news|title=FBI will try to rebuild Boston bombs|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/15/us/boston-marathon-investigation/index.html|last=Smith |first=Matt|coauthors=Josh Levs|publisher=CNN|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Fox News1"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Large police presence in Revere connected to Boston bombing|url=http://www.myfoxboston.com/story/21986273/large-police-presence-in-revere-connected-to-boston-bombing |publisher=[[WFXT]]|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref>

At least one of the devices was reportedly made from a [[pressure cooker]] packed with shards of metal, nails and bearing balls to inflict maximum casualties and was placed in a backpack.<ref name="CNN_FBI"/> The lid of one pressure cooker was found on a nearby rooftop.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ellement|first=John|title=Boston Medical Center reports five-year-old boy in critical condition, 23 victims treated from Boston Marathon bombings|url=http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/17/boston-medical-center-reports-five-year-old-boy-critical-condition-victims-treated-from-boston-marathon-bombings/gkKXBTqL2jyNhsC2Kz5GyO/story.html|accessdate=April 17, 2013|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=April 17, 2013|author2=Brian Ballou}}</ref> Investigators found remains of an electronic circuit board that was possibly used in the timer of the bomb.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57579766/boston-marathon-bombings-suburban-apartment-searched/ |title=FBI seeks images in Boston Marathon bomb probe; new details emerge on explosives |work=CBS News|date=April 16, 2013|accessdate=April 16, 2013}}</ref> [[Gunpowder]] was most likely used in the explosive devices.<ref name="Lister">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/16/us/boston-marathon-lone-wolf/|title=Boston Marathon bombs similar to 'lone wolf' devices, experts say|last=Lister|first=Tim|coauthors=Paul Cruickshank|date=April 17, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 17, 2013}}</ref>

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]], and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan International Airport]] remained open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry,<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Bomb Suspect Captured Alive in Backyard Boat|url=http://abcnews.go.com/US/one-boston-marathon-suspect-dead-second-run-police-say/story?id=18994511|author=Thomas, Pierre; Ross, Brian; Ferran, Lee; Curry, Colleen|date=April 19, 2013|work=ABC News|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St.<ref>{{cite news|title=Second Boston Marathon bombing suspect in custody|url=http://www.wcvb.com/Second-Boston-Marathon-bombing-suspect-in-custody/-/9849586/19814816/-/cw8b4az/-/index.html|date=April 20, 2013|work=WCBV.com|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a [[Miranda warning]], as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "[[public safety exception]]".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2013/04/next-for-bombing-suspect-high-value-detainee-interrogation-group/ |title=Feds Make Miranda Rights Exception for Marathon Bombing Suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev |work=[[ABC News]] |date=April 19, 2013 }}</ref>

===Other people identified or arrested as suspects===
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.3news.co.nz/LIVE-UPDATES-Police-hunt-for-Boston-bombing-suspect/tabid/417/articleID/294897/Default.aspx| title=LIVE UPDATES: Police hunt Boston bombing suspect| publisher=News 3 (New Zealand)| date=April 20, 2013}}</ref> Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.masslive.com/news/index.ssf/2013/04/reports_police_arrest_3_in_new.html| title=Police take 3 into custody in New Bedford at housing complex where Boston bombing suspect may have lived| publisher=MassLive.com| date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>
Suspects.plaintext:
Initial identification 
thumb|220px|right|FBI-released photo of suspects Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев), 26 years old, born October 21, 1986
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев), 19 years old, born July 22, 1993.

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The Tsranaevs also had two daughters, Bella and Amina. Tameraln and Dzhokhar emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer training at the Wai Kru Mixed Martial Arts 
Center, a Lowell club. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. According to a photo essay published by Johannes Hirn in 2010 in The Comment, the Boston University Graduate Student Magazine of Boston University's College of Communications, Tamerlan said then that he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the US Olympic team. He added that he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia". He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but a US permanent resident. He was married to American Katherine Russell, a Christian who had converted to Islam. The couple had a 3-year old daughter, Zahara. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan, he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture
thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Other people identified or arrested as suspects
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car. Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.

Suspects.plaintext:
Initial identification 

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев), 26 years old, born October 21, 1986
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев), 19 years old, born July 22, 1993.

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The Tsranaevs also had two daughters, Bella and Amina. Tamerlan and Dzhokhar emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer training at the Wai Kru Mixed Martial Arts 
Center, a Lowell club. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. According to a photo essay published by Johannes Hirn in 2010 in The Comment, the Boston University Graduate Student Magazine of Boston University's College of Communications, Tamerlan said then that he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the US Olympic team. He added that he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia". He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.  He was not an American citizen, but a US permanent resident. He was married to American Katherine Russell, who had recently converted from Christianity to Islam. The couple had a 3-year old daughter, Zahara. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Born in Kyrgyzstan, he became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Other people identified or arrested as suspects
Three men riding in a taxi were reported to have been arrested, and another man was reportedly forced to strip naked before being taken away, handcuffed and naked, in a patrol car. Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.
